newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on margin loan worries.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on margin loan worries.

text.p: Concerns over possible heavy selling pressure from margin loans took their toll on the Seoul bourse, sending the market to a shade lower close on Tuesday, brokers said.
The composite stock index shed 0.12 points to provisionally close at 781.76. Losers led gainers by 442 to 395.
"The market see-sawed throughout the day as investors differ in their views of demand and supply of stocks and its impact on the market," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
Brokers said an overhang of margin loans, scheduled initial public offering by LG Semicon and 14 million won worth rights issue offer pressured the market.

"With the current low level of market energy, investors shied away from large-cap shares to selective small-cap shares for quick gains," said Woo Sang-chul of Tongyang Securities. "The trend is expected to last until the Chusok holiday."
The Korean Thanksgiving holiday is from September 26 to 28.
Of highlighted small-cap shares, Seondo Electric went limit up, gaining 6,500 won to 117,500 and Keyang Elec also hit upper limit of 1,000 won to 18,000.
But steelmaker POSCO, which heavily weighted on the index, fell 500 won to 46,200. Samsung Electronics unchanged at 58,500.
But electricity monopoly KEPCO rebounded 200 won to 27,000 in reaction to recent consolidation.
On the eve of LG Semicon's initial public offering of 10 milion shares, LG Electronics added 300 won to 14,300. LG Electronics currently holds a 54 percent stake in the chip making unit.
Brokers said a record high closing on the Wall Street had no impact on the Seoul market due to local concerns.
They added investors shrugged off a decision by Korea's top business groups to freeze total spending on executive pay and benefits next year. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
